question: What is the minimum attendance I need in a bachelor course to avoid failing it automatically?
answer:
As a general rule, bachelor students must attend at least 80% of the sessions for each course [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 16, Article 15.1]. If your attendance falls below 80%, you will receive a fail grade of 0.0 in both the ordinary and extraordinary calls for that course [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2, Failing a course due to attendance].

Please note that academic heads of bachelor programs may require a higher level of attendance, including up to 100%, for specific academic activities [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 16, Article 15.2].

question: Does a medical appointment count as a justified absence under the bachelor attendance policy?
answer: No, a medical appointment is not considered a justified absence under the bachelor attendance policy [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2, Other Absences]. Such appointments are categorized as "other absences" and will count toward the maximum allowance of 20% total absences per course [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2, Other Absences].

Such appointments are categorized as "other absences" and will count toward the maximum allowance of 20% total absences per course [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2, Other Absences].

question: What is the pass mark for a bachelor course and how are the grade bands defined?
answer:
The pass mark for a bachelor course is five (5.0) [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 31, Article 33. “Official grading system”].

The grade bands are defined on a numerical scale from zero (0) to ten (10) as follows:
*   **0.0 - 4.9:** Fail (F)
*   **5.0 - 6.9:** Pass (P)
*   **7.0 - 8.9:** Very Good (VG)
*   **9.0 - 10:** Excellent (E)

[Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 31, Article 33. “Official grading system”]

question: How long does a bachelor professor have to communicate the grade of an assessment instrument?
answer: For bachelor degree programs, professors must communicate the grades from assessment instruments within at most fifteen (15) calendar days from the date of completion of the instrument during the teaching period, excluding official holidays [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 31-32, Article 35. “Reporting grades”].

question: How many ECTS credits must a bachelor student pass each academic year to be allowed to continue?
answer:
In each academic year, bachelor students must pass a minimum number of courses whose ECTS credits account for at least seventy percent (70%) of the ECTS credits established for that year in their degree programme [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 36, Article 45.4]. Failure to reach this 70% threshold means students may not continue their studies in the bachelor programme they are enrolled on [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 36, Article 45.5].

Additionally, for students enrolled from the 2025–2026 academic year onwards, there is a requirement to achieve a minimum annual Bachelor Score of 5.0; students who do not meet this score will be required to discontinue their studies, regardless of the number of ECTS credits passed [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 36-37, Article 45.7].

question: How many Honors Distinctions can be awarded in a bachelor course?
answer: A number of Honors Distinctions equivalent to 5% of all students on a bachelor programme who are enrolled on the same course may be awarded to students who achieve a grade equal to or higher than nine (9.0) "Excellent" [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 33-34, Article 39. “Honors Distinction”]. If the number of students enrolled on the course is less than twenty (20), only one Honors Distinction will be granted [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 33-34, Article 39. “Honors Distinction”].

If the number of students enrolled on the course is less than twenty (20), only one Honors Distinction will be granted [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 33-34, Article 39. “Honors Distinction”].

question: Can I ask for my final exam to be assessed by a board instead of only my professor?
answer:
Yes, you can ask for your final exam or assessment instrument to be assessed by a board (or committee) if it accounts for more than fifty percent (50%) of your final grade [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 30-31, Article 32. “Assessment boards”, Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 23, Article 30. Evaluation before a committee]. 

To do so, you must submit a request with duly substantiated reasons to your bachelor programme academic heads (or master's directors) at least seven (7) days before taking the assessment [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 30-31, Article 32. “Assessment boards”, Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 23, Article 30. Evaluation before a committee]. If approved, the board will consist of at least the course professor and another professor appointed by the academic heads or degree directors [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 30-31, Article 32. “Assessment boards”, Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 23, Article 30. Evaluation before a committee].

If the academic heads of the bachelor programmes agree to the request, the assessment shall be made by a board consisting of at least the course professor and another professor appointed by the academic heads of the bachelor programme. If the student does not agree with the decision of the academic heads of the bachelor programmes about the treatment of the request or the composition of the assessment board, the Vice-Rectorate responsible for academic affairs shall resolve the issue. 32.2. question: How many credits can the Academic Compensation Board compensate, and which courses can never be compensated?
answer:
For bachelor's degree programmes, students can appeal to the Academic Compensation Board for core and compulsory courses up to a maximum of five percent (5%) of ECTS credits, or up to a maximum of six (6) ECTS credits for compulsory courses of the last year [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 46, Article 62. “Access conditions and requirements”]. 

Under no circumstances are credits for the Final Project, internships, and elective courses eligible for compensation, nor are courses followed in International Mobility actions [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 46, Article 62. “Access conditions and requirements”]. 

*(Note: The provided master's degree regulations do not cover provisions for an Academic Compensation Board.)*

Under no circumstances are credits for the Final Project, internships, and elective courses eligible for compensation, nor are courses followed in International Mobility actions [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 46, Article 62. “Access conditions and requirements”]. 

*(Note: The provided master's degree regulations do not cover provisions for an Academic Compensation Board.)*

question: What is the deadline to ask the Rector for an additional examination session?
answer:
For bachelor degree students, a written request for an additional examination session must be submitted to the Rector within twenty (20) working days from the date for the finalization of student achievement records specified in the academic calendar, and only after all avenues for reviewing and appealing against grades have been exhausted [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 39, Article 47. “Additional examination session”].

The provided documents for Master Degree Programmes do not contain a provision for an additional examination session requested from the Rector. If you are a master student, please contact your Program Management through the Virtual Help Desk for clarification.

question: Where do I file a discrimination or harassment complaint at IE?
answer:
The Diversity Office (DO) is the single entry point for all discrimination and harassment complaints at IE University [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 22-23, IV.2. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL DISCRIMINATION AND/OR]. Any student is entitled to initiate a procedure regarding potential discrimination or harassment by any member of the IE community [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 22-23, IV.2. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL DISCRIMINATION AND/OR].

If the person involved in the alleged infringement is a faculty or staff member, students should submit a claim to the Harassment and Discrimination Intervention Line (HDI Line) managed by the Diversity Office [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 40, ANNEX III]. Additionally, incidences may be reported to the Diversity Commission via email at ComisiondeDiversidadeIgualdad@ie.edu [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Procedure].

question: On what grounds can I appeal a sanction in an academic integrity case?
answer:
You may appeal a sanction for an academic integrity violation based only on the following three grounds:

1.  If the process deviated from the rules set forth in the Student Code of Conduct.
2.  If new, previously unconsidered evidence emerges.
3.  If the sanction is clearly disproportionate to the offense, considering any aggravating or mitigating circumstances.

An appeal is not a *de novo* reconsideration of the entire case, nor is it an examination of the authority of the Program Direction or the AE Committee to hear the matter. The appeal is limited to considering whether any of these grounds are present to a degree sufficient to justify revising the decision [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 18-19, III.3. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL VIOLATIONS OF ACADEMIC].

question: Does the Student Code of Conduct apply to things I do off campus?
answer:
IE University expects compliance with its ethical standards from all students wherever they may be [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 5-6, II.2. SCOPE OF APPLICATION]. While students are generally not subject to judgment under the Student Code of Conduct for off-campus actions, there are two exceptions:

*   The conduct occurs in connection with an IE University-related program, event, or activity where the university exercised substantial control over the person and the context [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 5-6, II.2. SCOPE OF APPLICATION].
*   The conduct directly affects the IE Community’s welfare or core values, including its reputation, as determined by IE University management [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 5-6, II.2. SCOPE OF APPLICATION].

question: If a master's student passes a subject in the extraordinary call, what is the highest grade they can get?
answer: If a master's student passes a subject in the extraordinary call, the grade is limited to a five (5.0) "pass" or "aprobado" [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 29, Article 42. Ordinary and extraordinary calls].
raw_answer: If a master's student passes a subject in the extraordinary call, the grade is limited to a five (5.0) "pass" or "aprobado" [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 29, Article 42. Ordinary and extraordinary calls].

question: How are internal US-style grades distributed in master's programmes?
answer: In master's programmes, master’s directors may apply an internal US-type grading system that distributes grades according to the following curve: the top 15% receive Honors, the next 35% receive Excellence, the next 35% receive Proficiency, and the lowest 15% receive a Pass [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, pp. 20-21, Article 25. Assessment]. A Fail is assigned to students who fall below the minimum threshold, which is established as the group's mean minus twice the standard deviation [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, pp. 20-21, Article 25. Assessment].

question: Do master's students who study in Spanish need to prove their English level?
answer: Yes, all master's students studying in Spanish must obtain an accreditation of an intermediate academic and professional level of spoken and written English to complete their program [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, pp. 9-10, Article 11.6]. If English is the student's native language, they are exempt from this requirement [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, pp. 9-10, Article 11.6]. Accepted certifications and details regarding exemptions will be communicated by the master’s directors to students before the start of the enrollment process [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 10, Article 11.6].

question: What do I have to include when I disclose that I used AI in an assignment?
answer:
When you use AI in an assignment, you must be transparent and disclose the following information [Student Guidelines on AI (v4), p. 3, Transparency]:

*   **Platforms used:** Identify the specific AI-powered tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Grammarly, Canva, Gemini).
*   **Usage explanation:** Explain how the tools were used (e.g., brainstorming, proofreading, language polishing, or generating visuals).
*   **Prompts:** Document the prompts you used so that faculty can evaluate your proficiency in collaborating with AI if requested.
*   **Visuals:** Clearly indicate any images, videos, graphics, or conceptual maps generated by AI and reference the tool used.

Failure to properly disclose AI usage is considered academic misconduct [Student Guidelines on AI (v4), p. 4, Submitting work created by someone or]. You should also check your course syllabus, as faculty may restrict or prohibit AI use for specific assignments [Student Guidelines on AI (v4), p. 1, We are working continuously with our faculty to].

question: If I fall below 80% attendance in a bachelor course, what happens to my grade, and could it affect whether I can continue at IE?
answer:
If your attendance in a bachelor course falls below 80%, you will receive a fail grade of 0.0 in both the ordinary and extraordinary calls for that course [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2, Failing a course due to attendance]. Both of these failing grades will appear on your academic record and will count toward your Bachelor Score [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2, Failing a course due to attendance]. 

Regarding your ability to continue at IE, the documents state that attendance below the required level means you cannot pass the course in the examination sessions for the academic year [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 16, Article 15. “Attending academic activities in the programme”]. If you have concerns about how this may impact your progression, you should contact your Program Management team through the Virtual Help Desk.

question: How do I challenge a final grade in a bachelor course, and what are the deadlines?
answer:
To challenge a final grade in a bachelor course, you must first review the grade with the professor responsible for the course [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 32-33, Article 37.1]. After this review, if you wish to proceed, you may file a written substantiated appeal with the academic heads of the bachelor programmes [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 32-33, Article 37.1].

The deadline for filing this appeal is no later than five (5) working days during the teaching period following the conclusion of the review period for grades in each examination session [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 32-33, Article 37.1].

question: How do the attendance rules differ between a bachelor course and a master's subject?
answer:
Both bachelor and master programs generally require students to attend at least 80% of sessions, though program directors may set different or higher requirements [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 16, Article 15.1-15.2; Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 12, Article 15.1-15.2].

The primary difference lies in the consequences of failing to meet these requirements:

*   **Bachelor Programs:** If a student's attendance falls below the required level without authorization, they cannot pass the course in either the ordinary or extraordinary examination sessions and will receive a final grade of zero (0.0) "Fail" for that academic year [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 16, Article 15.3; Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2].
*   **Master Programs:** If a student's attendance falls short of the required level without proper approval, the consequences are defined in the syllabus for that specific subject [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 12, Article 15.3].

question: A bachelor student fails a core course in both the ordinary and the extraordinary calls. What happens next, and when would they be unable to continue?
answer:
If a bachelor student fails a course in both the ordinary and extraordinary examination sessions, they must enroll in the course again in the following academic year, unless the case falls under specific exceptions [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 37-38, Article 46.6].

Regarding the ability to continue studies, students who fail a programme course in the examination sessions and under the conditions set out in the regulations may not continue their studies in the programme they were enrolled in at IE University [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 42-43, Article 55.1]. Additionally, all students must achieve a minimum annual Bachelor Score of 5.0; those who do not achieve this score are required to discontinue their studies at IE University, regardless of the number of ECTS credits passed or examination sessions completed [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, pp. 36-37, Article 45.7].

question: I have a court summons on the day of a bachelor exam. Is my absence justified and can I take the exam another day?
answer:
An official summons to testify before a court is considered a justified absence, provided supporting documentation is submitted through the Virtual Help Desk within seven (7) days [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, pp. 1-2, Justified Absences]. 

Regarding taking the exam another day, the Academic Regulations state that the application of rules regarding missing an exam can be waived by the academic head of the bachelor programme in the event of a duly demonstrated cause that prevented participation in assessment instruments [Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes, p. 38, Article 46. “Ordinary and extraordinary examination sessions”]. You must contact Program Management via the Virtual Help Desk to manage this request, as faculty members are not authorized to approve absences or exam arrangements [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, pp. 1-2, Justified Absences, p. 2, Additional Provisions].

question: How long can an academic integrity case take, and how long do I have to appeal the decision?
answer:
For cases handled by the Program Direction, the decision must be communicated to the student within thirty (30) business/academic days from the date the student was informed of the potential infraction [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 17, III.3. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL VIOLATIONS OF ACADEMIC]. For cases handled by the Academic Ethics Committee, the committee will communicate its decision within fourteen (14) business/academic days from the date of the committee meeting [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 18, III.3. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL VIOLATIONS OF ACADEMIC]. These timelines may be extended if exceptional circumstances occur [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 17, III.3. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL VIOLATIONS OF ACADEMIC; The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 18, III.3. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL VIOLATIONS OF ACADEMIC].

You must present an appeal within five (5) business/academic days from the date the decision is notified to you [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 19, III.3. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL VIOLATIONS OF ACADEMIC]. Appeals must be resolved by the respective appeal body within an additional period of ten (10) business/academic days from the date the appeal is presented, though this timeline may also be extended in exceptional circumstances [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 19, III.3. PROCEDURES FOR POTENTIAL VIOLATIONS OF ACADEMIC].

question: If a master's student's attendance falls below 80% in a subject, what grade do they get in the ordinary call, and can they still take the extraordinary call?
answer:
If a master's student does not comply with the attendance requirements, the grade in the ordinary call will be between zero and four-point-nine (0–4.9) "Fail" [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, pp. 29-30, Article 42. Ordinary and extraordinary calls]. The academic director of the degree may waive this rule in the event of serious illness or other duly accredited causes that prevented the student from participating in educational activities and assessment exercises [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, pp. 29-30, Article 42. Ordinary and extraordinary calls]. 

Regarding the extraordinary call, the regulations state that if a student does not pass a subject in the ordinary call, an extraordinary call will take place, except for cases expressly mentioned [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 29, Article 42. Ordinary and extraordinary calls]. Please note that the document provided for Bachelor programs regarding automatic failure in both calls does not apply to Master's students [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, p. 2, Failing a course due to attendance].

question: Is a documented job or internship interview a justified absence for a master's student?
answer: I can't find this in the IE documents. The *Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes* state that master's directors may partially exempt students from attendance for "duly justified reasons" and will assess each case individually [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 12, Article 15.4]. While the *Attendance Policy* for Bachelor programs explicitly lists job or internship interviews as justified absences, this policy does not apply to master's students [Attendance Policy, Bachelor Programs, pp. 1-2, Justified Absences]. Please contact your Program Management through the Virtual Help Desk to confirm how to handle your specific situation.

question: I am absent from a master's in-person class but join it online. Am I still marked absent, and can I take that day's exam?
answer:
Whether you are marked absent when joining an in-person class online depends on the specific conditions detailed in the subject's syllabus [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 14, Article 17.5]. In general, attendance and participation for subjects taught partially online are recorded by technical means adapted to the teaching model, and the syllabus must specify how these criteria are applied [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 14, Article 17.5].

Regarding exams, if you do not complete an evaluation exercise without a justified reason, you will be considered as not passing and will obtain the lowest grade [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 23, Article 29.4]. Students who are unable to perform a scheduled evaluation exercise for a sufficiently justified reason have the right to complete it at a different time [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 23, Article 29.4]. Justifications for missing an evaluation are governed by the same rules established for attendance and participation [Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes, p. 23, Article 29.5].

You should consult your subject's syllabus for specific attendance rules and contact your program management through the Virtual Help Desk if you have concerns about your specific situation.

question: How do I report a harassment incident at IE, and where do I send it?
answer:
To report a harassment incident, the procedure depends on the nature of the situation:

*   **General Harassment:** You should report the incident by email or letter addressed to the Diversity Commission at ComisiondeDiversidadeIgualdad@ie.edu, including a list of the facts [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Procedure].
*   **If a Faculty or Staff Member is involved:** Students should submit a claim to the Harassment and Discrimination Intervention Line (HDI Line) platform [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 40, ANNEX III]. If the matter is not resolved through mediation, you may request that the HDI Office refer the case to the Compliance Office at ComplianceOffice@ie.edu [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 40, ANNEX III].

question: In an informal harassment procedure, how soon must the Diversity Commission meet the parties, and how long does it have to produce its report?
answer: In an informal harassment procedure, the Diversity Commission must arrange a meeting with the parties involved within a maximum of 5 days of the verbal or written presentation of the complaint [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Interviewing the parties involved]. Once the interview has been held, the Commission must prepare an informal report stating the results of the investigation and the proposed solution within a maximum of 3 working days [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Interviewing the parties involved].

question: What conditions must be met for behavior to count as moral harassment (mobbing) under the harassment code?
answer:
Under the Code for the Prevention of Harassment, moral harassment (mobbing) is defined as a situation where a person or group of persons behaves in a hostile or intimidating manner toward another, provided the following conditions are met:

*   The behavior occurs systematically (at least once a week) [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Description].
*   It takes place over an extended period (more than 6 months) [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Description].
*   It occurs in the workplace or an extension thereof [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Description].

Additionally, the behavior involves physical and/or psychological actions aimed at making the victim give up their position or deriving pleasure from the victim's suffering [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 2, Definition of unacceptable behavior].

answer: More than 95% of the total amount of waste entering the plants is recycled or reused [Environmental Policy, p. 4]. The final waste processor is the specialised waste management company GRUPO DEFESA [Environmental Policy, p. 4].

Finally, waste disposal is outsourced to the specialised waste management compan y GRUPO DEFESA. This company’s procedures have been certified with the ‘Zero Waste’ stamp. This means all the waste that enters their plants is further segregated categorically , resulting in more than 95% of the total amount being recycled or reused and not ending in a landfill. Thus, the total waste generated at IE University is closely equal to the total amount of waste recycled. The remainder is a small quantity and is composed of unrecyclable items. Defesa’s ‘Zero Waste’ certificate is attached at the end of this policy as Annex 2. The pure organic waste disposed is separated from inorganic municipal solid waste through a triage process carried out at the Defesa treatment plant and is further recycled through a biomethanisation and composting process. For further reduction, IE University has put in place an initiative to cut food waste. Through a collaboration with the company TooGoodToGo, the leftover perishable food from the cafeteria is redistributed with a discounted price. Due to the nature of its activities, IE University generates negligible hazardous waste.

question: Who can start a harassment complaint at IE, and what does IE say about who may investigate it?
answer:
A harassment complaint can be initiated by the worker who has allegedly been harassed or by any person who has witnessed harassment or behavior that contradicts the Code for the Prevention of Harassment [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Procedure]. If a student is the affected person, they should submit a claim to the Harassment and Discrimination Intervention Line (HDI Line) [The IE Student Code of Conduct, p. 40, ANNEX III].

Regarding investigations, the Diversity Commission assigns a person to study the case, who is responsible for listening to, processing, and investigating the complaint [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Procedure]. When a faculty or staff member is involved, the HDI Office or the Compliance Office may conduct the investigation, potentially including external advice [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 40-41, ANNEX III]. Furthermore, the Professional Diversity & Equality Commission (PDEC) may investigate or designate an individual to do so [The IE Student Code of Conduct, pp. 40-41, ANNEX III]. All persons investigating these complaints must have no previous connection with any of the parties involved [Equal Opportunities and Diversity Plan, p. 3, SEXUAL HARASSMENT AND DISCRIMINATION].

question: Which initiatives do IE's policy documents use to cut single-use containers and food waste on campus?
answer:
To reduce single-use containers and food waste, IE University has implemented the following initiatives:

*   **Single-use containers:** The university has partnered with the company Bumerang to introduce a system of loaned reusable food containers in the cafeteria to cut the use of disposable take-away packaging [Environmental Policy, pp. 2-4; Climate and Sustainability Plan (CASP v3), p. 8, OBJECTIVE WHY IT MATTERS KPI'S].
*   **Food waste:** IE University collaborates with TooGoodToGo to redistribute leftover perishable food from the cafeteria at a discounted price [Environmental Policy, p. 4; Climate and Sustainability Plan (CASP v3), p. 8, OBJECTIVE WHY IT MATTERS KPI'S]. Additionally, on the Segovia campus, the university composts approximately 20 kilograms of food waste every week [Climate and Sustainability Plan (CASP v3), p. 8, OBJECTIVE WHY IT MATTERS KPI'S]. 

Furthermore, the university employs recycling stations for organic waste, plastic, paper, glass, and batteries, and outsources waste disposal to a company with a "Zero Waste" certification, which ensures that more than 95% of waste is recycled or reused [Environmental Policy, pp. 2-4].

• IE University sources 100% of its electricity from certified renewable providers and achieved carbon neutrality for its direct operational emissions in 2022, positioning itself among the first universities in Europe to reach this milestone. • Through the 10 Year Challenge, IE has driven continuous improvements in operational efficiency, upgrading HVAC and water systems with smart technologies and embedding real-time energy management tools like the "Hubgrade" platform across its campuses. • IE University has implemented annual third-party audits to verify its greenhouse gas emissions, reinforcing the credibility of its climate strategy. Finally, waste disposal is outsourced to the specialised waste management compan y GRUPO DEFESA. This company’s procedures have been certified with the ‘Zero Waste’ stamp. This means all the waste that enters their plants is further segregated categorically , resulting in more than 95% of the total amount being recycled or reused and not ending in a landfill. Thus, the total waste generated at IE University is closely equal to the total amount of waste recycled. The remainder is a small quantity and is composed of unrecyclable items. Defesa’s ‘Zero Waste’ certificate is attached at the end of this policy as Annex 2. The pure organic waste disposed is separated from inorganic municipal solid waste through a triage process carried out at the Defesa treatment plant and is further recycled through a biomethanisation and composting process. For further reduction, IE University has put in place an initiative to cut food waste. Through a collaboration with the company TooGoodToGo, the leftover perishable food from the cafeteria is redistributed with a discounted price. Due to the nature of its activities, IE University generates negligible hazardous waste.

At IE University, we embrace this role with urgency and vision, forging new paths toward a sustainable and inclusive future. Guided by our core values, the IE University Sustainability Office works to cultivate a sustainability-driven culture by raising awareness, inspiring behavior change, and integrating sustainability into decision-making. Through active engagement, data-driven strategies, and transparent reporting, we strive to reduce emissions. At IE University, we embed sustainability across our campus and beyond. Our dedication extends to preparing future leaders who will transform industries, economies, and policies in response to the climate crisis. At the heart of this plan are six key goals that encompass our approach to climate action: • Transformative Knowledge and Skill Development • Sustainable Campus Operations • Leading Research on Grand Challenges • Social Equity • Community Engagement • Governance and Ethical Leadership Each goal in this plan translates into measurable action. It is not just a roadmap for compliance; it is a forward-looking vision designed to transform our institution into a leader in sustainability, empowering students and staff to create a lasting, positive impact.

question: How many harassment complaints did the Diversity Commission receive last year?
answer: I can't find this in the IE documents. While the *Code for the Prevention of Harassment* states that the Diversity Commission keeps a confidential register of complaints, the documents do not provide statistics or the number of complaints received in any specific year [Code for the Prevention of Harassment, p. 3, Procedure]. Please contact Program Management through the Virtual Help Desk for further information.

The procedure will be set in motion at the petition of the worker who has allegedly been harassed, or any person who has witnessed harassment or behavior that contradicts this code and reports said behavior. 1. Incidences should be reported by e-mail or letter addressed to the Diversity Commission, complete with a list of the facts. The e-mail address for reporing such incidences is: ComisiondeDiversidadeIgualdad@ie.edu 2. The Diversity Commission will assign a person to study the case and will take the measures it considers appropriate, including the need to inform the Executive Committee and/or the Risk Prevention Service. The person assigned to the case will proceed as follows: • Listen, receive, process and investigate any complaint of alleged harass ment that is presented in person or in writing. • Arrange to meet the parties involved, take statements and establish facts. • Present a report on the results of his/her investigation. • Propose preventative and corrective method for conflict situations. • Monitor the results of the agreement and apply further corrective mea sures, for which purpose he or she may enlist the help of another person.

Specific action against harassment of a sexual and discriminatory nature. 5.1.1.
